result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.descendants_at_distance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Find the nodes exactly a given number of hops from a source. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.descendants_at_distance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Find the nodes exactly a given number of hops from a source. title: >- [Graph.descendants_at_distance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Find the nodes exactly a given number of hops from a source. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the nodes exactly a given number of hops from a source. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L55606-L55665){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.descendants_at_distance( source, distance, mode="out", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Descendants at distance](/assets/graphs/descendants-at-distance.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A five-node tree laid out in columns by hop distance from A (outlined), from d=0 to d=3: A joins B, B joins C and D, and D joins E. C and D, exactly two hops away, are shaded in the accent color with the edges that reach them; E, three hops away, is faded. The card lists C, D." width="100%"} Returns the nodes whose shortest-path distance (in hops) from `source` is exactly `distance`: the "friends of friends" at distance 2, the nodes three stops away, and so on. It is one layer of `bfs_layers()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The start node, as an ID or label. [distance]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The number of hops (`0` gives the source itself). [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge direction to follow on directed graphs: `"out"` (default), `"in"` or `"all"`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [set[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node IDs at that distance (empty if there are none). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the source does not exist or `mode` is invalid. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} A breadth-first search stopped at the requested layer, $O(V + E)$ at most. Matches NetworkX's `descendants_at_distance`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#3bff0d22 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("D", "E")]) sorted(g.get_label_from_id(n) for n in g.descendants_at_distance("A", 2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['C', 'D'] ``` ::: :::
